methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $575M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
VulcanForms is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Hart and Martin Feldmann that has raised $575M+ to date. The broader robotics and manufacturing sector includes 9 comparables—1 public and 8 private—though a sufficiently tight peer set of same-stage or adjacent-stage companies does not exist to support conventional median multiple triangulation.

Given data constraints, the Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable framework. Using total capital raised ($575M) as a value proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Late Stage to the subsequent financing round yields $690M. This method rests on the assumption that capital deployed correlates with embedded value creation at this stage, though the multiplier itself reflects market-observed step sizes rather than company-specific metrics.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $586M to $793M, centered on $690M. The range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the point estimate, acknowledging execution and market condition risk. Key uncertainties include the absence of tightly comparable late-stage peers, the lack of disclosed revenue or EBITDA multiples, and reliance on a single methodological input. A more precise valuation would require either access to recent comparable transaction data within robotics manufacturing or disclosure of VulcanForms' operating metrics.
